report:
Fresh complete followup review of anchor_pages. Saved/read prior report and inputs, then started fresh and recaptured all dependencies. Every initial fragment is unchanged: claim, whole anchors.rs implementation, ordinary integration test and TODO test. Three helper ranges are unchanged in both position and content. The anchor_url helper moved from spec.rs 575-579 to 576-580 due to a preceding association comment; I located the current function and verified its newly captured contents exactly equal the prior intended helper. No helper behavior or page behavior changed. This corrects the positional capture without blindly refreshing unrelated content.

The full claim requires stable rule pages, definition/context, implementation and test evidence, Rust excerpts and surrounding-source access, per-entry placeholder status/explanation and individual inspectability of multiple sites. The ordinary page implementation and its captured whole-file helpers generate pages from the canonical anchor/evidence inventory; namespace children include rules that also have descendants, and anchor_url derives a stable route from the dotted name. Generated pages have no canonical source copy. page displays the full name, definition, source filename, canonical context and breadcrumbs. It emits one section per implementation and indexed test rather than collapsing sites into aggregate badges. Implementations retain module/target/location/cfg/excerpt/status/reason; test fragments are selected by file/crate/target/Rust identity and display the complete function with contained explanation comments and status/cfg. Both receive surrounding-source explorer links. The captured escape/URL helpers keep content literal and route payloads encoded. Missing associations are labeled as validation errors; review state and report are separate from source evidence and imply no run. Namespace aggregates supplement these individual sections.

The complete ordinary generated_anchor_pages_join_namespaces_claims_implementations_tests_and_reviews test uses a real temporary workspace and preprocess executable. It supplies an ordinary and TODO site for one rule and N/A child/sibling sites. Assertions check generated rule/namespace paths, parent-rule-with-child structure, null canonical source, context links, implementation/test excerpts, surrounding-source link, individual TODO/N/A reasons and status attributes, accepted/changes-requested/unfinished reviews, requested-edit text and escaped multiline report. It also requires exactly three canonical definitions after rendering. The recaptured Fixture creates real files and invokes production preprocessing, and chapters rejects duplicate paths. This provides meaningful representative multi-site evidence, not a badge-only assertion.

The sole TODO canonical_anchor_pages remains explicit test deferral, with no behavioral assertions. Its comprehensive stable-page/all-sites/excerpts/status/reason matrix is not silently completed by the representative integration test. Retiring it requires assertions enumerating all sites/statuses plus stability and destination/excerpt navigation cases; browser interaction is not established by the current Rust test. It is a coverage prerequisite, not an assertion that the current page implementation is absent. No N/A entries exist for this anchor.

All full-claim aspects remain accounted for by the current source/assertions or visible TODO after verifying the actual range shift and unchanged content against the prior complete assessment. No source edits, build, browser or test runs occurred; this review used start/read/record and source inspection. No requested edits.
